source.publication: 2025 PIT-RES Resident Individual Income Tax Return Instructions and Form PIT-RES 2025; tax rate schedule from 30 Del. C. §1102(a)(14)
source.section: Instructions PDF p.6 Line 6 Pension Exclusion (under-60 rules, 60-or-over worksheet lines 1-4, eligible retirement income, NOTE, example); Instructions PDF p.8 Line 21 Additional Standard Deduction items 1-5; Form PIT-RES Lines 1-12, 20a-24, 26-27b, 32-33; Instructions PDF p.5 Line 1; PDF p.8 Line 20a standard deduction table, Line 24, Line 27a; PDF p.9 Line 27b; tax rate schedule 30 Del. C. §1102(a)(14) (record brackets cite)

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (spouse) 50,000.00 + ira distribution (spouse) 3,000.00 + private pension (you) 5,000.00 + interest 2,000.00 + dividends 1,000.00 = 61,000.00. Federal taxable income = 61,000.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 - 1 x 1,600.00 additional for age 65 or older = 27,900.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form PIT-RES (filing status 2 joint, Column B): Line 1 federal AGI 61,000.00; Line 2 other states' obligations interest 0.00; Line 3 0.00; Line 4 total 61,000.00. Line 5 U.S. obligations interest 0.00. Line 6 pension exclusion, you (age 66): worksheet line 1 pension 5,000.00; line 2 half the joint-account interest 1,000.00 + half the dividends 500.00 = 1,500.00; line 3 6,500.00; line 4 lesser of 6,500.00 and 12,500.00 = 6,500.00. Line 6 pension exclusion, spouse (age 62): worksheet line 1 pension 0.00 (no pension needed: PDF p.6 example); line 2 IRA 3,000.00 + half the interest 1,000.00 + half the dividends 500.00 = 4,500.00; line 3 4,500.00; line 4 lesser of 4,500.00 and 12,500.00 = 4,500.00. Line 6 total = 6,500.00 + 4,500.00 = 11,000.00. Line 7 0.00; Line 8a 0.00; Line 8b 0.00. Line 9 (Lines 5-8b) = 11,000.00. Line 10 = 61,000.00 - 11,000.00 = 50,000.00. Line 11 0.00 (Line 11 worksheet: combined earned income is 50,000.00, so no). Line 12 Delaware AGI = 50,000.00. Line 20a standard deduction (filing status 2) 6,500.00; Line 21 additional standard deduction 1 box(es) for 65 or over x 2,500.00 = 2,500.00; Line 22 = 9,000.00. Line 23 taxable income = 50,000.00 - 9,000.00 = 41,000.00. Line 24 tax, §1102(a)(14) schedule as numbers: 2.2% x 3,000.00 = 66.00 + 3.9% x 5,000.00 = 195.00 + 4.8% x 10,000.00 = 480.00 + 5.2% x 5,000.00 = 260.00 + 5.55% x 16,000.00 = 888.00; total 1,889.00 (the Division's tax table, not in the sources, would give a row figure; expected keeps the formula). Line 25 0.00; Line 26 = 1,889.00. Line 27a personal credits 2 x 110.00 = 220.00; Line 27b additional credits 2 box(es) for 60 or over x 110.00 = 220.00; Line 32 total non-refundable credits 440.00. Line 33 balance = 1,889.00 - 440.00 = 1,449.00. Joint accounts are split equally (PDF p.6 example); any other split of the 3,000.00 of interest and dividends leaves both spouses under 12,500.00, so the total exclusion is 11,000.00 however the projection attributes them. Only the 66-year-old gets the Line 21 additional 2,500; both get Line 27b.
